brief: A stand to hold a 60-litre fish tank full of water.

requirements.evidence: 7 full bases with full top covers forming one 453x475mm flush deck at 80mm high (deckOf 7 covers). check_build clear, capped and locked.
requirements.requirement: Stand platform sized to hold a 60-litre tank footprint

requirements.evidence: Parts are 3D-printed plastic and the configurator checks fit only; it knows nothing about strength or load ratings. 60L of water alone is ~60kg plus glass/substrate. Cannot verify this build will carry that.
requirements.requirement: Safely support 60 litres full of water in service

requirements.evidence: Same reason: material/waterproofing not checked by configurator; user chooses material. Shape gives flat support only.
requirements.requirement: Water resistance / material suitability for aquarium use

finish.summary: Built a low 7-cell capped platform as a tank support shape, but it cannot be rated to carry a 60L full tank (~60kg+). Load/strength and waterproofing are unverified in this system — use a manufactured aquarium stand rated for the weight.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: A 60-litre tank is heavy when full — I'll check what the stand can and can't promise and shape a base for it.

result.note: Ask again with a family or a few words (text) to see the parts themselves.

events.text: That weight can't be verified in plastic here, so I'll build the stand shape and mark the load requirement accordingly.
